brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Kilnroom, the online shop in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: handmade and warm but not rustic or folksy; no pottery wheels, no vase or mug silhouettes, no flames. It must work on a shipping label, a tissue-paper sticker and Instagram. Web and social only; customers in Turkey and Europe.

claim.notes: Eleştirmen üç yöne (threshold, maker-seal, room-k) iki eskiz turunda da none verdi, hiçbir konsept kapıya ulaşmadı; sıradaki yön tek kil yastığında üç olgunlaşma konisi.

concepts.title: Maker's Seal
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a bitten cookie / Pac-Man blob, at 16 px an eye; s2 a triangle in a blob, warning sign or guitar pick, the cone is too stiff to read as a cone; s3 a fat letter C / croissant, wrong letter; s4 three white wedges in a rounded box, fries, candles or teeth, at 16 px a crown. Struck s1-s3. s4 holds the only ownable idea, a witness-cone pack showing one firing, but its cones are rigid tilted triangles, so nobody reads them as melting. Next move: draw the cone pack the way potters know it, three tapered cones set at an angle in a clay pad, the last one actually slumping (tip curving down toward the pad, tapering, not a constant-width hook). Keep the cones as the positive shape and drop the generic pebble container. Use the pad/seal edge only if it stays a real stamp outline, then test at 16 px against fries/crown.

concepts.title: Room K
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a rounded K with a notch bitten from the stem, the initial with a cut; s2 a K in a rounded geometric sans with a slightly offset leg, the initial with an offset; s3 a plain rounded-sans K, a stock font letter. All three strike: initial with a cut/offset, or a typeset K with no hook. Rounded-terminal sans also reads app/UI rather than handmade. This direction has had two passes with no ownable device. Retire it, or fold the K into a wordmark rather than a symbol.

concepts.title: Threshold
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a lowercase r, also a cane or question mark, wrong letter; s2 an underscore plus r, a terminal prompt; s3 the registered-trademark sign (r in a circle), a fatal known mark; s4 two bars and an r, at 16 px 'llr' or a bar chart. The bent cone is drawn as a constant-width hook, so it reads as an r every time. s4's progression (upright, upright, slumped) is the right story, a firing told by witness cones, but the slump needs a real cone: a tapered body whose tip droops below its shoulder toward the base, all three cones planted in one pad at a shared lean so they read as a set, not letters. Avoid any circle container (the ® reading). Consider merging with maker-seal s4.
